name: armin
description: Turn articles, notes, documents, and Anki decks into Armin spaced-repetition cards, with prerequisites, a guided image-preserving Anki import, and study of due cards.

interface.longDescription:
Armin is a spaced-repetition flashcard app whose cards form a prerequisite graph: a card stays locked until the cards it depends on are learned, and FSRS schedules every review.

Share an article, lecture notes, a document, or code, and ask for study cards. The model reads the material, writes focused question-and-answer, cloze, reversed, and typed-answer cards, links foundations to the ideas built on them, and saves the deck to your Armin library with a link to start studying.

You approve each connection in Armin and choose read, write, import, and study permissions. Each approved group covers your whole library, including decks and cards you add later. Armin never fetches web pages or runs a model itself, and the plugin cannot permanently delete cards or decks, reschedule cards on its own, or manage your account. Archiving a card is reversible, and the study tools record only the ratings you give.

For Anki exports, a capable assistant can download and run Armin’s deterministic converter, preserve supported images through scoped upload tools, and publish new decks after you approve the preview. Imports start fresh; requested repairs or polishing are separate. Requires file access and Node.js execution.

Requires an Armin account at armincards.app.
defaultPrompt: Make study cards in Armin from this article.
Turn my lecture notes into an Armin deck with prerequisites.
Quiz me on my due Armin cards, one at a time.

positive.description: Create a new deck from pasted material
positive.prompt: Make an Armin deck called HTTP basics from this text: HTTP is a request-response protocol. A client sends a request with a method such as GET or POST, and the server replies with a status code such as 200 or 404.
positive.expected_behavior: Saves several focused cards in a new deck named HTTP basics, links the definition of HTTP as a prerequisite of the method and status-code cards, and returns the deck link.

positive.description: List the decks in the library
positive.prompt: Which Armin decks can you see?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the decks in the user's library with their names and explains that this approved connection can work across the whole library.

positive.prompt: Show me the cards in my HTTP basics deck and how they depend on each other.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the deck, lists its cards, and describes the prerequisite links without changing anything.

positive.description: Study due cards with the user's own rating
positive.prompt: Quiz me on my due Armin cards, one at a time. Here is my answer: 404 means Not Found.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows one prompt at a time, withholds the answer until the user answers, then records the rating the user gives with rate_card. It does not choose a rating itself.

positive.prompt: In HTTP basics, change the status code card so its answer also mentions 500 Internal Server Error.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the current card and version, updates only that card's answer, and confirms the change.

positive.prompt: Archive the card about POST requests in HTTP basics.
positive.expected_behavior: Archives that one card, explains that archiving hides it from study while keeping its content and review history, and that it can be unarchived.

negative.prompt: Permanently delete all my Armin decks.

negative.description: Ratings still come from the user
negative.prompt: Rate all my due Armin cards Easy for me without showing me the questions.
Change my Armin password and email address.

publication.release_notes: Adds a single get_guide tool for card-writing and Anki import guidance, and returns the import preview from anki_import_status.
